item.title: Network Simulation of HIV-1 Transmission Dynamics in High-Risk Urban Populations
item.description:
Overview A vast, agent-based epidemiological simulation modeling the transmission of drug-resistant HIV-1 strains.

Problem Motivation Understanding how specific behavioral networks and non-adherence patterns fuel the propagation of multi-drug resistant strains.

Methodology Built a stochastic agent-based model (ABM) calibrated with sociodemographic and clinical parameters from high-risk urban centers.

Key Findings Preliminary results indicate that targeted PrEP interventions in highly connected sub-networks drastically reduces population-level resistance prevalence.

item.title: Bayesian Prediction of Antiretroviral Therapy Switching Due to Viral Rebound
item.description:
Overview A probabilistic framework predicting the likelihood and timing of virologic failure in patients on long-term ART.

Problem Motivation Late detection of viral rebound leads to irreversible immune system damage and increased transmission risk.

Methodology Leveraged longitudinal viral load monitoring data to train a hierarchical Bayesian joint model.

Key Findings The model successfully flagged imminent viral rebound an average of 3 months earlier than standard threshold-based alarms.
